_note: The climate accord, V3.5: a fifth org on the V3.2 register, and the first whose founding rule is DERIVED rather than inherited -- the members are the EU-27 (every loaded nation but GBR and CHE), the same roster the eu carries, because a climate club the EU's neighbours stand outside is the one shape the register had no way to say before a fifth org existed. Seats are NATO's own rule, round(population / 1e6) over the committed nation files, summing to exactly 452 (pinned in tests/test_orgs.gd); FRA's 69 are 15.3 percent of the council, which is what makes the player one voter among many rather than its owner. accession_seats 17 is the AUTHOR's call at the plan gate, 2026-09-10: the EU-27 mean seat count, the same compromise the authored tables make for small members -- a GBR or CHE accession votes with 17 too. accession 18 / withdrawal 24 months: joining is faster than the eu's Art. 50 shape, leaving is not. Bonuses zero-priced on the eurozone/schengen precedent -- a standing co-member price needs its own measured band, and the named trigger is the first adopted proposal that prices one; until then relations and gravity read the accord's membership not at all, which is the bit-identity property T8's re-run prediction leans on. The accession and withdrawal positions are MEASURED, not felt: Referendum.yes_share() was swept over the two-axis grid at a neutral-approval new-game by tools/climate_probe.gd table (c), and both questions sit 0.010-0.023 above the strict majority at rest -- accession (-0.2, +0.3) reads 0.5177, withdrawal (-0.05, +0.15) reads 0.5179, both mid-band on a plateau of in-band neighbours rather than on the cliff the band's right edge turned out to be (the only right-of-centre in-band cell reads 0.5101, one ten-thousandth above the floor) -- winnable by a president the country does not hate, losable by one it does. At rest the sweep is nation-independent (the referendum reads only global bloc tables and the neutral approval every new game seeds), so GBR and CHE read the same number for the same position; the probe prints both columns to prove it rather than assume it. V4.5b: the presidency is the real rotating order, Council Decision (EU) 2016/1316, anchored at Estonia's 2017-H2 term -- 27 six-month terms, one full cycle to Malta's 2030-H2. No order after 2030 is published, so the game repeats the cycle from Estonia: a recorded content bound, not a forecast (France's next in-game presidency is 2035-H2). Decisions default to qualified majority; a proposal that is treaty-class says so itself. The accord shares the eu's order and anchor because it sits under the EU Council's environment formation: whoever chairs the Union chairs the accord.
name: The Climate Accord
summary: The bloc's shared emissions ceiling and the fund that pays for the transition: members accept one measured line per head, and answer to the others for the gap.
